slides.title: This is where it begins.
slides.text: Before any app, any account, any data, there is you, and the phone in your hand.

slides.title: You tap.
slides.text: You touch your {passkey}, the key that lives on your phone. No password, nothing to type. The tap says: it's really me.

slides.title: Something wakes up.
slides.text: With that tap, your passkey whispers a {secret} to theOS. The same secret every time, and theOS never writes it down. Tap again tomorrow, and it whispers it again.

slides.title: From the secret, a pen.
slides.text: theOS shapes the secret into your {pen}. Whatever you write with it carries your signature, and nobody can copy that signature.

slides.title: And a padlock.
slides.text: From the same secret comes your {padlock}. You can hand open copies to anyone. Whatever they lock with it, only you can open.

slides.title: You write your first page.
slides.text: With your pen you sign a single page: “this is my pen, and this is the fingerprint of my next one.” It is your {birth page}, and you write it only once.

slides.title: That page becomes your name.
slides.text: theOS takes the fingerprint of your birth page. That fingerprint is your {ID}: who you are from now on. Nobody can fake it, and it stays yours even if your pen changes one day.

slides.title: Now you can keep things.
slides.text: Your ID opens a place that is yours. Every note, message or photo you put there is an {entry}: its own small box, signed with your pen.

slides.title: Every box has its own key.
slides.text: Each box is locked with a fresh, tiny {entry key}. If one were ever lost, it would open that one box and nothing else.

slides.title: The tiny key goes into an envelope.
slides.text: You put the entry key into an {envelope} and lock it with your padlock. Now only you can get the key back out.

slides.title: A friend wants to see it.
slides.text: You don't copy the box. You add a second envelope, locked with your friend's padlock: one box, two envelopes. Take that envelope away later, and your friend gets nothing new.

slides.title: Out in the world.
slides.text: Servers and peers carry your boxes and envelopes to every device. They can store them, copy them and pass them on, but never open them, and never forge one in your name.

slides.title: Tomorrow, you tap again.
slides.text: Same passkey, same secret, same pen and padlock. Your ID opens your place, your envelopes give back your keys, and every box opens again. That is theID.
